text:
Let that door close

that will not let me be alone with your kisses.

Let that door close

through which fields, sun, and roses wish to see us.

That door through which

the blue limewash of the pillars comes in

to look, like mischievous children,

at the shyness of our two caresses

that do not give themselves because of the door, open…


For serene reasons

we spend a long time with the door open.

And it is risky to kiss

and press each other’s hands, even

to look too much at each other, even

to keep silent in fair contest…


But at night

the door falls upon itself

and closes so blindly and clearly

that you and I feel ourselves in open country,

choosing caresses like jewels

hidden in nights with gardens

laid on the knees of mountains,

but alone, you and I.

The soft penumbra

links our bodies and plunders

my untried tenderness,

the strength of my arms that overwhelm you

so sweetly, the great insatiable kiss

that drinks itself

and in its space redeems

the smallness of boundless distances…


Happy door that accompanies us

closed, in our happiness. Your obstruction

is the liberation of these two prisons;

the escape route of the two footsteps

identical, that leap into the cloud

from which one returns in the morning.

translation.title: Let That Door Close
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the door’s paradoxical role as obstacle and liberation, along with the long, sensuous central stanza.
